title: Shaky Hands: Causes, When to Worry and the Blood Tests That Check
summary: Shaky hands or a hand tremor? See what the shaking pattern suggests, when to get urgent care, and how TSH, glucose and metabolic tests check the cause.
body_markdown:
Table of contents


**Shaky hands are most often an exaggerated version of the small tremor everyone has, made visible by caffeine, stress, anxiety, fear, fatigue or smoking** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]. This kind of shaking comes and goes with its trigger and is not a sign of disease \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


**Shaking that is new, lasting or getting worse has a short list of common causes** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]: essential tremor, an overactive thyroid, low blood sugar, side effects of medicines, alcohol withdrawal and Parkinson disease. When the hands tremble, a doctor first asks when it happens (at rest or during movement), where it is (one hand or both) and how it looks \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. Blood tests then check the medical causes: a TSH test for the thyroid, a glucose test and HbA1c for blood sugar, and a metabolic panel for the liver and kidneys \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]. Essential tremor and Parkinson disease are diagnosed with an exam, not a blood test \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \].


## When shaky hands need urgent care


**Call 911 right away if shaking comes with sudden numbness or weakness in the face, arm or leg, especially on one side of the body** \[[6](https://www.cdc.gov/stroke/signs-symptoms/index.html) \]. Stroke is one of the listed causes of tremor \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \], and these are signs of stroke. The other sudden signs are \[[6](https://www.cdc.gov/stroke/signs-symptoms/index.html) \]:


- confusion, trouble speaking, or trouble understanding speech;
- trouble seeing in one or both eyes;
- trouble walking, dizziness, loss of balance or lack of coordination;
- a severe headache with no known cause.


The CDC’s B.E. F.A.S.T. check helps: loss of **B** alance, **E** ye changes, a drooping **F** ace when the person smiles, one **A** rm that drifts down when both are raised, slurred **S** peech, and **T** ime to call 911 \[[6](https://www.cdc.gov/stroke/signs-symptoms/index.html) \]. Do not drive to the hospital or let someone drive you. An ambulance team can start treatment on the way \[[6](https://www.cdc.gov/stroke/signs-symptoms/index.html) \].


**Also get emergency help for** :


- **Severe low blood sugar.** Shaking, sweating and hunger that do not improve after eating something with sugar, or a person with diabetes who becomes less alert, cannot be woken, or has a seizure. Call 911 or get a ride to the emergency room, and do not drive yourself \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \].
- **Alcohol withdrawal with danger signs.** Shaking after stopping heavy drinking, together with seizures, fever, severe confusion, hallucinations or an irregular heartbeat \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \].
- **Overactive thyroid with danger signs.** A change in consciousness, dizziness, or a rapid, irregular heartbeat in someone with thyroid symptoms \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \].


None of these should wait for a blood test. The tests in this article are for shaking that comes and goes or builds slowly, never for sudden symptoms.


**See a provider soon, not urgently, if the tremor** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]:


- is worse at rest and gets better when you reach for something;
- lasts, is severe, or interferes with your life;
- comes with headache, weakness, abnormal tongue movements, muscle tightening or other movements you cannot control.


## Reading the pattern: rest or movement, one hand or both, constant or in episodes


**When the shaking happens, where it is, and whether it comes in episodes narrow the cause before any test.** Doctors divide tremor into two kinds: rest tremor, which happens when the hand is relaxed and supported, and action tremor, which happens when you use the hand, hold it out or reach for something \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


Pattern Likely causes What checks it


Both hands during movement, such as writing or holding a cup, building slowly over years, often running in the family Essential tremor \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \] A clinician’s exam and history. Blood tests are usually normal \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]


At rest, easing when the hand moves, often one hand first, sometimes a “pill-rolling” motion Parkinson disease \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \] A neurological exam. No blood test diagnoses it \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]


A fine tremor of both hands, with a racing heart, sweating, heat intolerance or weight loss Overactive thyroid \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]\[[10](https://www.thyroid.org/hyperthyroidism/) \] TSH, then free T4 and T3 if TSH is abnormal \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]


Episodes with hunger, sweating, a pounding heart or unclear thinking, easing after food Low blood sugar \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]\[[12](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/low-blood-glucose-hypoglycemia) \] A glucose reading during an episode. HbA1c shows whether diabetes is present \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]\[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]


Fine shaking of both hands after coffee, during stress, or after poor sleep Caffeine, stress, anxiety or fatigue \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]\[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html) \] The pattern itself. It fades as the trigger passes \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]


Starting within a day or so of stopping heavy drinking Alcohol withdrawal \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \] Prompt medical care \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \]


Starting after a new medicine or a dose change A medicine side effect \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \] Review with the prescriber \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]


With confusion, drowsiness or yellow skin, and a “flapping” of the hands held out Severe liver disease \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000302.htm) \] Urgent care. Liver tests and other blood tests \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000302.htm) \]


Sudden, with weakness on one side, a drooping face or trouble speaking Stroke \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[6](https://www.cdc.gov/stroke/signs-symptoms/index.html) \] Call 911


**Constant versus episodes matters.** A tremor from a neurological condition such as essential tremor or Parkinson disease is present most days and changes slowly \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]. Shaking that arrives in clear episodes, such as a few hours after a meal, after coffee, or during a stressful moment, points to a trigger that comes and goes, such as low blood sugar, caffeine or anxiety \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]\[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html) \]\[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000924.htm) \]. Shaking from these triggers, from medicines, from alcohol withdrawal and from an overactive thyroid is called enhanced physiologic tremor. It is a fine tremor of both hands and fingers, and it can go away once the cause is corrected \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


## Essential tremor


**Essential tremor is the most common type of tremor** \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. It is a shaking of the hands and forearms that shows up mostly during movement, such as writing, drawing, drinking from a cup or using tools, and is less noticeable at rest \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. The shaking is small and fast, at 4 to 12 movements a second \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \], and it can also affect the head, voice or eyelids \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \].


Typical features of essential tremor are \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]:


- it usually affects both hands, but not always the same way on each side;
- it often runs in families, and NINDS reports it is inherited in 50 to 70% of cases;
- it most often first appears in adolescence or middle age, between 40 and 50, and is most common after 65;
- it gets worse with stress, caffeine, lack of sleep and certain medicines;
- it may improve slightly after a small amount of alcohol, which is not a recommended treatment and carries a risk of alcohol use disorder.


**Essential tremor is diagnosed from a physical exam and your history, and blood tests and brain scans are usually normal** \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. Tests are used to rule out other reasons for the shaking: an overactive thyroid, alcohol withdrawal, too much caffeine, smoking, certain medicines, and nervousness or anxiety \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. That is why a TSH test is a common early check even when essential tremor seems likely. Essential tremor is not dangerous, although severe shaking can interfere with writing, eating and drinking \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. StatPearls describes it as benign with regard to life expectancy \[[17](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499986/) \].


## Parkinson disease and other neurological causes


**Parkinson tremor usually appears when the hand is at rest and goes away when the hand moves** \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]. It can look as if someone is rolling a pill between the thumb and a finger, and it often starts in one hand or on one side of the body before spreading \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. Not everyone with Parkinson disease has a tremor \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


Parkinson disease most often develops after age 60 \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]. Besides the tremor, it causes \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]:


- slowed movements and trouble starting to move, such as getting out of a chair;
- rigid or stiff muscles;
- problems with balance and walking;
- smaller, harder to read handwriting;
- a quieter voice and less facial expression.


**No blood test diagnoses Parkinson disease.** A provider diagnoses it from the symptoms and a physical exam, and may run tests to rule out other conditions with similar symptoms \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]. A brain scan called a DaTscan is needed only in some situations \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \].


Other neurological causes of tremor include multiple sclerosis, stroke, dystonia (muscles that tighten on their own), damage to the cerebellum, and exposure to heavy metals such as mercury, manganese or lead \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. These are also diagnosed with a neurological exam and, when needed, imaging \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


## Caffeine, stress, anxiety and sleep


**Too much caffeine can cause restlessness and shakiness** \[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html) \], and NINDS notes it can cause a temporary tremor or make an existing one worse \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. Some people are more sensitive to caffeine than others \[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html) \]. Caffeine is in coffee, tea, cola drinks and chocolate, and is added to some pain relievers, cold medicines and alertness products \[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html) \].


**Stress, anxiety, fear and fatigue make the normal hand tremor more noticeable** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. Trembling or shaking is one of the listed symptoms of a panic attack, along with a pounding heart, sweating and numbness or tingling in the hands \[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000924.htm) \]. This shaking comes with the anxious moment and settles as it passes. For how anxiety and low mood can overlap with blood results, see[anxiety and low mood: what your blood might be telling you](https://mitohealth.com/blog/anxiety-and-low-mood-what-your-blood-might-be-telling-you) .


**Sleep matters too.** Some tremors get worse when a person is tired, and getting enough sleep is one of the standard self-care steps for tremor of any cause \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]\[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \].


Anxiety and shaking can both come from an overactive thyroid \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]\[[10](https://www.thyroid.org/hyperthyroidism/) \], so new anxiety with a tremor that does not ease when you are calm is worth a TSH test (see below).


## Low blood sugar


**Shaking or trembling is one of the first symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)** \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. NIDDK lists feeling shaky or jittery among the mild to moderate symptoms, along with hunger, tiredness, dizziness, irritability and a fast heartbeat \[[12](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/low-blood-glucose-hypoglycemia) \]. Sweating, headache, feeling nervous, blurry vision and tingling skin are other common signs \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \].


Blood sugar below 70 mg/dL is considered low \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. Symptoms tend to come on quickly \[[12](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/low-blood-glucose-hypoglycemia) \]. Milder symptoms such as hunger and sweating appear when blood sugar is only slightly low, while unclear thinking or a seizure can happen when it is much lower, below 54 mg/dL \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. For the full list, see[symptoms of low glucose](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-glucose) .


**Low blood sugar is most common in people with diabetes who take insulin or certain other diabetes medicines** \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]\[[12](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/low-blood-glucose-hypoglycemia) \]. In people without diabetes, it can be caused by drinking alcohol, some medicines, a lack of hormones such as cortisol or thyroid hormone, severe heart, kidney or liver failure, some types of weight-loss surgery and, rarely, a tumor of the pancreas \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. NINDS notes that both high and low blood sugar may cause tremors \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


**The test that confirms low blood sugar is a[glucose](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/glucose) reading taken while the symptoms are happening** \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. A single fasting glucose, which is also part of a comprehensive metabolic panel, shows your level at one moment \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \].[HbA1c](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/hba1c) shows your average blood sugar over about the last 3 months and is the main test for diabetes and prediabetes \[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]:


- below 5.7% is normal;
- 5.7% to 6.4% is prediabetes;
- 6.5% or higher is diabetes.


If shaky episodes keep happening, a provider may ask you to wear a glucose monitor for a few days to catch lows you would otherwise miss \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. Mito offers an[HbA1c blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/hemoglobin-a1c-with-reflex-to-1-5-anhydroglucitol-1-5-ag) and a[fasting glucose test](https://mitohealth.com/products/glucose-fasting) .


## Overactive thyroid


**Hand tremor is one of the common symptoms of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)** , a condition in which the thyroid makes too much hormone and the body’s processes speed up \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]\[[10](https://www.thyroid.org/hyperthyroidism/) \]. On exam, a doctor often finds shaking of the hands and very strong reflexes \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \].


The tremor usually comes with other signs of a sped-up body \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]\[[10](https://www.thyroid.org/hyperthyroidism/) \]\[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]:


- a racing, pounding or irregular heartbeat;
- feeling hot and sweating more;
- anxiety, nervousness, irritability and trouble sleeping;
- weight loss despite a normal or bigger appetite;
- more frequent bowel movements;
- lighter or less frequent periods.


Symptoms can start suddenly or come on slowly \[[10](https://www.thyroid.org/hyperthyroidism/) \]. Adults over 60 may have different symptoms, such as losing their appetite or withdrawing from other people \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]. Graves disease is the most common cause, and inflammation of the thyroid after pregnancy is a common one \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]. Taking too much thyroid hormone medicine can also cause it \[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]. For how Graves disease differs from the more common underactive thyroid, see[Hashimoto’s vs Graves’ disease](https://mitohealth.com/blog/hashimotos-vs-graves-disease-autoimmune-thyroid-testing-and-key-differences) .


**A[TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone)](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/thyroid-stimulating-hormone) blood test is the first check** \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]. When the thyroid makes too much hormone, the pituitary gland makes little or no TSH, so an overactive thyroid usually shows up as a low TSH \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]. A TSH result shows whether the thyroid is making too much or too little hormone, but not why \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]. If TSH is abnormal, the next tests are usually free T4 and T3, and thyroid antibodies to look for Graves disease \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]\[[9](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000356.htm) \]. For what a TSH number means, see[what TSH in a blood test means](https://mitohealth.com/guide/what-is-tsh-in-blood-test) , and for the symptoms of high thyroid hormone levels, see[symptoms of high T4](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-high-t4) and[symptoms of high T3](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-high-t3) .


A tremor from an overactive thyroid usually improves once the thyroid problem is treated \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]. Mito offers a[TSH blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/thyroid-stimulating-hormone-tsh) . For which thyroid tests to add after TSH, see[the best thyroid test for you](https://mitohealth.com/guide/best-thyroid-test) .


## Medicines and alcohol withdrawal


**Several kinds of medicine can cause a tremor** , including certain asthma medicines, corticosteroids, chemotherapy, and drugs used for some psychiatric and neurological conditions \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. A tremor that starts after a new medicine or a dose change is worth raising with the prescriber. Do not change or stop a medicine on your own \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \].


**Alcohol withdrawal causes shaky hands when someone who drinks heavily and regularly suddenly stops** \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \]. Symptoms usually start within 8 hours of the last drink, though they can start days later, and tend to peak by 24 to 72 hours \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \]. Shakiness comes with anxiety, sweating, a rapid heart rate, nausea and trouble sleeping \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \]. Alcohol withdrawal can quickly become life-threatening: contact a provider right away or go to an emergency room if you think it is happening, and call 911 for seizures, fever, severe confusion, hallucinations or an irregular heartbeat \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \]. Long-term heavy drinking can also damage the cerebellum, the part of the brain that coordinates movement, and cause a slower tremor \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


## Liver, kidneys and electrolytes


**Liver failure and kidney failure can affect brain areas that control movement and cause tremors or jerky movements** \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. In severe liver disease, toxins the liver no longer clears can affect the brain. One sign is a “flapping tremor” of the hands when the arms are held out in front of the body, along with confusion, drowsiness, slurred speech or yellow skin and eyes \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000302.htm) \]. This needs urgent medical care.


**A comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) checks the liver and kidneys in one blood draw** , along with blood glucose and electrolytes such as sodium, potassium and calcium \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]. Labs use its[creatinine](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/creatinine) result to estimate kidney function \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]. Mito offers a[Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)](https://mitohealth.com/products/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp) .


**Calcium works differently from magnesium.** The listed symptoms of a low calcium level are muscle cramps, spasms or stiffness and tingling in the lips, tongue, fingers and feet. Shaking is not among them \[[18](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/calcium-blood-test/) \]. Many people with an abnormal calcium level have no symptoms, so it is often found on a routine test such as the CMP \[[18](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/calcium-blood-test/) \].


## Magnesium and vitamin B12


**Low magnesium (hypomagnesemia) is a deficiency with a direct link to shaking: its signs range from mild tremors and generalized weakness to, in severe cases, heart problems** \[[19](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK500003/) \]. Other symptoms of low magnesium are muscle cramps or spasms, fatigue, weakness and numbness \[[20](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000315.htm) \]\[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/magnesium-blood-test/) \]. Common causes include alcohol use, long-term diarrhea, poorly controlled diabetes, malabsorption such as celiac disease, and some medicines, including diuretics and proton pump inhibitors for stomach acid \[[20](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000315.htm) \]\[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/magnesium-blood-test/) \].


Magnesium is not part of the standard CMP. It is measured with its own[magnesium blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/magnesium) , and the normal range is 1.6 to 2.6 mg/dL, though ranges vary slightly between labs \[[20](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000315.htm) \]\[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/magnesium-blood-test/) \]. A magnesium test also helps explain low potassium or calcium levels, so the three are often checked together \[[20](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000315.htm) \]\[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/magnesium-blood-test/) \]. For the full list of signs, see[symptoms of low magnesium](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-magnesium) and[signs of magnesium deficiency](https://mitohealth.com/blog/signs-of-magnesium-deficiency) .


**Low vitamin B12 damages nerves, but its listed nerve symptoms are numbness and tingling in the hands and feet, loss of balance and trouble concentrating, rather than a rhythmic tremor** \[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000574.htm) \]. If your hands feel unsteady because they are numb or you cannot feel what you are holding, or you also have tingling or balance problems, a[vitamin B12 test](https://mitohealth.com/products/vitamin-b12-cobalamin) is a reasonable check. For tingling as the main symptom, see[tingling in hands](https://mitohealth.com/blog/tingling-in-hands) , and for the vitamin itself, the[vitamin B12](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/vitamin-b12) marker page.


## How to stop shaking hands


**There is no single fix, because the right step depends on the cause.** Shaking from a medical condition, such as an overactive thyroid, will likely get better when the condition is treated \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]. For the common triggers:


- **Possible low blood sugar.** If you have diabetes and feel shaky, sweaty and hungry, check your blood sugar and follow the plan your provider gave you, which usually means juice, another sugary drink, food or glucose tablets \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]. If the symptoms do not improve after eating something with sugar, call 911 or get a ride to the emergency room \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \].
- **Caffeine.** Avoiding or cutting back on caffeine is recommended for tremor of any cause \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].
- **Stress and anxiety.** Relaxation, meditation or breathing exercises can help tremor caused by stress \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \].
- **Tiredness.** Getting enough sleep is recommended for tremor of any cause \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].
- **A medicine.** Talk to the prescriber about a change. Do not stop a medicine on your own \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \].
- **Alcohol.** Alcohol is not a recommended treatment for tremor, even though a small amount can briefly ease essential tremor \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]. If shaking started after stopping heavy drinking, get medical care \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000764.htm) \].


**Practical tricks steady the hands for daily tasks** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]\[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]: drinking from a half-filled cup or through a straw, using utensils that are heavier or have larger handles, and wearing a heavier bracelet or watch, which may reduce a hand or arm tremor.


A tremor may not need treatment unless it interferes with daily activities or causes embarrassment \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]. When it does, a provider can discuss medicines and other treatments for the specific type of tremor \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \].


## Which blood tests check the cause of shaky hands


**MedlinePlus lists the blood tests a provider may order for tremor: a complete blood count, thyroid function tests and a glucose test, alongside urine tests and, when needed, nerve tests and brain imaging** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003192.htm) \]. NINDS adds that blood or urine samples help rule out contributing factors \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]. Each result points in a different direction:


Result What it suggests


Low TSH An overactive thyroid is likely. Free T4 and T3 come next \[[11](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/) \]


Glucose below 70 mg/dL during shaky symptoms Low blood sugar \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]


HbA1c of 6.5% or higher Diabetes. Low blood sugar happens most often in people with diabetes who take insulin or certain other medicines \[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]\[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000386.htm) \]\[[12](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/low-blood-glucose-hypoglycemia) \]


HbA1c of 5.7% to 6.4% Prediabetes \[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]


Abnormal liver tests or kidney function on a CMP Liver or kidney disease may be contributing \[[2](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/tremor) \]\[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]


Magnesium below the normal range Low magnesium, which can cause mild tremors \[[19](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK500003/) \]\[[20](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000315.htm) \]


Low vitamin B12 B12 deficiency, which mainly causes numbness, tingling and balance problems \[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000574.htm) \]


All normal The common blood causes are less likely. Essential tremor and Parkinson disease are diagnosed by exam \[[4](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000762.htm) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000755.htm) \]

- **[TSH blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/thyroid-stimulating-hormone-tsh) .** The first check for an overactive thyroid, a listed cause of hand tremor that a blood test can confirm.

## Frequently asked questions


### What vitamin deficiency causes shaking hands?


Low magnesium is the deficiency most directly linked to shaking: mild tremors are among the listed signs of a low blood magnesium level, along with weakness and muscle cramps. Magnesium is a mineral rather than a vitamin. Low vitamin B12 mainly affects nerves in a different way, causing numbness, tingling and loss of balance rather than a rhythmic tremor. A magnesium blood test and a vitamin B12 test check both. Caffeine, stress, an overactive thyroid and low blood sugar are more common causes of shaky hands than a vitamin deficiency.


### When should I worry about shaky hands?


Call 911 if shaking comes with sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, a drooping face, trouble speaking or seeing, or a sudden severe headache, which are stroke signs. Also call 911 if shakiness from low blood sugar does not improve after eating something with sugar, or the person becomes less alert or has a seizure. See a provider soon for a tremor that is worse at rest, that keeps getting worse, that interferes with daily life, or that comes with a racing heart, weight loss, stiffness or slowed movement.


### How do I stop my hands from shaking right away?


The quickest fix depends on the cause. If you have diabetes and feel shaky, sweaty and hungry, check your blood sugar and eat or drink something with sugar. If coffee or stress is the trigger, cutting back on caffeine, slow breathing and relaxation help, and the shaking fades as the trigger passes. Holding a cup half full, using utensils with larger handles and wearing a heavier watch or bracelet can steady the hands. Do not stop a prescribed medicine on your own, and do not use alcohol to calm a tremor.


### What disease starts with hand shaking?


Essential tremor and Parkinson disease are the two neurological conditions most often first noticed as hand shaking. Essential tremor usually affects both hands during movement, such as writing or holding a cup. Parkinson tremor usually appears when the hand is resting, often in one hand first, and comes with stiffness and slowed movement. An overactive thyroid often shows up with a fine hand tremor too, along with a racing heart, sweating and weight loss. A clinician diagnoses essential tremor and Parkinson disease with an exam, while a TSH blood test checks the thyroid.


### Can anxiety cause shaky hands?


Yes. Stress, anxiety, fear and fatigue can all make the small tremor everyone has more visible, and trembling or shaking is one of the listed symptoms of a panic attack. This kind of shaking comes with the anxious moment and settles as it passes. Shaking that continues when you are calm, or that comes with weight loss, a racing heart or heat intolerance, is worth checking with a TSH test, because an overactive thyroid causes both anxiety and hand tremor.
